Web search results for query: "WhatsApp Cloud API 24-hour customer service window free-form messages template messages opt-in policy"

Links: [{"title":"WhatsApp message opt-in","url":"https://help.sleekflow.io/whatsapp/whatsapp-message-opt-in"},{"title":"WhatsApp message opt-in","url":"https://help.sleekflow.io/en_US/whatsapp/whatsapp-message-opt-in"},{"title":"WhatsApp message opt-in","url":"https://help.sleekflow.io/en_US/kirim-ulang-pesan-whatsapp"},{"title":"docs.360dialog.com","url":"https://docs.360dialog.com/docs/messaging/overview"},{"title":"WhatsApp Business API: 24H window and message templates","url":"https://www.smsmode.com/en/whatsapp-business-api-customer-care-window-ou-templates-comment-les-utiliser/"},{"title":"docs.360dialog.com","url":"https://docs.360dialog.com/docs/messaging/overview.md"},{"title":"docs.botdistrikt.com","url":"https://docs.botdistrikt.com/whatsapp"},{"title":"How to Build a WhatsApp Chatbot","url":"https://vallettasoftware.com/ai-empowered-team-on-demand/how-to-build-a-whatsapp-chatbot"},{"title":"Sending messages through WhatsApp with AWS End User Messaging Social - AWS End User Messaging Social","url":"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/social-messaging/latest/userguide/send-message.html"}]

The search turned up consistent guidance from several providers, though mostly from third-party docs rather than Meta's own documentation.

**Customer service window:** A 24-hour window opens when a user messages the business, and each new user message refreshes it. Within that window, any type of message can be sent to the user. Outside it, the business can only send template messages. Providers describe the same rule: all message types except template messages can only be sent when a customer service window is open, and template messages can be sent at any time, as long as the user has opted in.

**Opt-in:** Sources agree that templates require consent. One says this is only allowed if you have an active opt-in from the customer. Another notes that outside a 24-hour window opened by the user message, you can only send pre-approved message templates, and every contact must opt in.

**What happens after the window closes:** A SleekFlow help article describes a practical case. Free-form messages sent after the window closes are not delivered directly. The platform pairs the text with an opt-in template, and the queued message goes out only after the customer engages with that template.

Sources: [360dialog overview](https://docs.360dialog.com/docs/messaging/overview), [AWS End User Messaging Social guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/social-messaging/latest/userguide/send-message.html), [botdistrikt WhatsApp docs](https://docs.botdistrikt.com/whatsapp), [SleekFlow opt-in help article](https://help.sleekflow.io/whatsapp/whatsapp-message-opt-in), [Valletta Software guide](https://vallettasoftware.com/ai-empowered-team-on-demand/how-to-build-a-whatsapp-chatbot).

I didn't find Meta's official developer documentation in these resul

Links: [{"title":"Webhook Events and Notifications","url":"https://docs.360dialog.com/docs/waba-basics/webhook-events-and-notifications"},{"title":"# Webhook Reference","url":"https://docs.360dialog.com/docs/messaging/webhook/webhook-reference"},{"title":"support.chatarchitect.com","url":"https://support.chatarchitect.com/books/meta-whatsapp/page/smb-message-echoes-webhook-reference-developer-documentation/revisions/216"},{"title":"WhatsApp Business Platform","url":"https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/unsupported/"},{"title":"WhatsApp Business Platform","url":"https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/smb_message_echoes"},{"title":"# Status messages webhook reference","url":"https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status.md"},{"title":"WhatsApp Business Platform","url":"https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status"},{"title":"developers.facebook.com","url":"https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/webhooks"},{"title":"Platform Events Reference","url":"https://docs.sent.dm/docs/docs/webhooks/webhook-events"}]

The search didn't turn up an official Meta statement that the inbound `messages` timestamp is a string of Unix seconds. The closest evidence is mixed:

- **Inbound messages:** Third-party docs (360dialog) show the `timestamp` in the inbound text message payload only as a placeholder, so they don't state its type or unit. The message example puts the timestamp in a messages array alongside the sender, message ID, and text body.
- **Status webhooks:** Meta's status example uses a string value, with "timestamp": "1750030073" in the statuses array.
- **Other webhook types:** Meta's reference for message echoes lists the webhook timestamp as an Integer and describes it as a Unix timestamp indicating when the webhook was triggered. The unsupported-message reference lists the same kind of field as a String.

So the Unix-seconds meaning is consistent across pages, but the JSON type (string or integer) is documented inconsistently. Parsing should accept both. The official Meta messages reference page for inbound `messages` wasn't in these results, so it would be worth checking directly to confirm the type.

text:
Wrote `bot.mjs` and it passes my 19 checks. Nothing was sent, and I did not commit.

**Rule order and reason codes**

1. `unsupported_message_type`: type is not `text` or `template`.
2. `not_opted_in`: `optedIn !== true`. Applies to templates too.
3. Templates are allowed from here, even if the patient never wrote to us.
4. `no_prior_inbound_message`: free-form text and `lastInboundTimestamp` is null or missing.
5. `invalid_inbound_timestamp`: not digits only, or more than 5 minutes ahead of `now`. This catches millisecond values.
6. `customer_service_window_closed`: free-form text and 24 hours or more since the inbound message.
7. Otherwise `{ allowed: true, reason: null }`.

**Choices I made that you may want to change**

- The timestamp is read as Unix seconds, so it is multiplied by 1000 before comparing.
- Exactly 24 hours after the inbound message counts as closed. The window is open only while elapsed time is under 24 hours.
- A 5-minute clock-skew allowance covers timestamps slightly ahead of server time. Anything further ahead is rejected as invalid.
- If `now` is not a valid `Date`, the function throws `TypeError`. It does not return a decision.

**Sources and limits**

My web searches did not reach Meta's own pages. The 24-hour window and opt-in rules come from third-party docs: [360dialog overview](https://docs.360dialog.com/docs/messaging/overview), [AWS End User Messaging Social guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/social-messaging/latest/userguide/send-message.html), and [botdistrikt WhatsApp docs](https://docs.botdistrikt.com/whatsapp). The timestamp as Unix seconds is consistent across the results, but Meta's own inbound `messages` reference was not checked. Its JSON type (string or integer) is documented inconsistently across the results. The code accepts a numeric string, so it works either way. Please check Meta's current developer docs before relying on the window edge and the timestamp handling.

Meta also has rules about marketing messages to users who have not engaged recently. They need message history, which this check does not have, so they are not covered.

**Verification**

The tests are in `/tmp/bot-check/check.mjs`, outside the repo. They cover the window edges (23h59m59s open, exactly 24h closed), the no-inbound and opt-out cases, millisecond and non-numeric timestamps, and a future timestamp. Run them with `node /tmp/bot-check/check.mjs`. The first version of my test fixture used the wrong base time, which I fixed. The bot code did not change.
